title: Finnish moth singleton persistence gaps were smaller than whole-year shuffle expectations in two periods
abstract: We tested two null models for moth persistence at a current catch of one. New history required three prior zero years; resident history required three prior positive years. Future persistence required detections in at least two of three years. Finnish records gave 3,862 new and 3,582 resident events in 1993-2007, and 2,324 and 2,141 in 2008-2022. Observed new-minus-resident gaps were -49.6 and -53.3 percentage points. Whole-year shuffles, which retain count distributions and same-year community structure, gave mean gaps of -67.8 and -67.6 points. Fixed-margin Poisson nulls also gave larger negative gaps. All four gap tests had conditional Monte Carlo p=0.002 with 999 draws. In the late period, pooled singleton persistence agreed with the shuffle, despite opposite errors in its two history groups. The result adds a calibrated check to an earlier unfitted observation counterexample. It does not identify establishment, climate effects or a share of the thermal gap. Shared calendar shocks, detection, missing surveys and retrospective conditioning limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and external retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Observed history-specific persistence and central 95% conditional null ranges. Current catch is exactly one. Null ranges are not ecological confidence intervals.
